newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight eases slightly, market remains tight.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight eases slightly, market remains tight.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate eased slightly to 8.50/60 percent from 8.60/70 percent on Monday, with the market still short of funds, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said bids by banks and finance companies seeking fresh funds kept the overnight rate above eight percent.
The overnight traded between 8.40 and 8.80 percent.
"The overnight is still high as the market remains short," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
In the morning, other interbank rates remained firm despite further injection of funds by Bank Negara Malaysia.
Dealers said the central bank was again seen lending one-month money at 8.50 percent.
The current squeeze was caused by some month-end ringgit demand, they said.
One-month money was steady at 8.50 percent while three-month was also unchanged at 8.30 percent.
Bank Negara is said to have injected funds over the past two weeks to help ease market tightness.
Recent heavy buying of the ringgit by the central bank to defend the currency from speculative attack had caused a liquidity squeeze.
There was no confirmation of the funds injection from Bank Negara, which does not usually comment on its market operations.
Dealers said rates were likely to come off following maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday and another one billion ringgit next week.

Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange rebounded after recent falls on expectations that interbank rates would come down soon now that the ringgit has stabilised, futures market dealers said.
At 0800 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up six points to 92.30, or an implied yield of 7.70 percent.
The December contract rose three to 92.52, or 7.48 percent while March 1998 was up four to 92.62, or 7.38 percent.
